The confidentiality provisions in the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) weren't made for your "right to privacy." They were to prevent the free market from creating an information-economy out of your medical records, which could hinder your ability to carry the same medical coverage from one job to another.

Protecting your privacy is only a side-effect of the provisions, but not their primary intent. Violations of the provisions carry severe criminal penalties, so it's easy to mistake HIPAA for some kind of super-hero fighting for you. But it's just a pile of severe regulations trying to suppress a stock market of medical records from springing up and screwing with your ability to get insured at rates you used to pay before you got AIDS.
